facts.text: The hotel is located inside the Iguassu park, which gives guests up to six additional hours to explore beyond the park's 9-5 opening hours for other visitors.
facts.excerpt: Whilst all other visitors must adhere to the strict 9-5 opening hours, our location inside the park gives our guests up to six additional hours of freedom to explore.

facts.text: There are no other buildings for miles around the hotel.
facts.excerpt: There are no other buildings for miles around.

facts.text: The hotel has a colonial tower that rises above the trees.
facts.excerpt: our colonial tower protruding through the trees

facts.text: The hotel has a pink facade.
The hotel building dates from 1958 and is a Portuguese colonial-style building in delicate pink.
facts.excerpt: the 1958-built Das Cataratas is an elaborate Portuguese colonial–style building in delicate pink

facts.text: Das Cataratas is the only hotel within Iguacu National Park in Brazil, according to Conde Nast Traveler.
Floors are dark wood and bathrooms are finished in white marble.
facts.excerpt: Floors are made of rich dark wood and bathrooms finished in white marble.

facts.text: Beds are dressed in Egyptian cotton.
facts.excerpt: Beds are dressed in crisp Egyptian cotton

facts.text: The hotel has an infinity pool.
The gardens are planted with orchids and bromeliads.
facts.excerpt: stroll through gardens bejeweled by orchids and bromeliads

facts.text: The spa sources its treatment ingredients from the surrounding jungle.
facts.excerpt: Ingredients are sourced in the surrounding jungle; our treatments draw on the delights of the Amazon.

facts.text: The bar serves a Devil's Throat cocktail, named after the horseshoe waterfall.

facts.text: A hotel guide offers bio-tours of the park's fauna.
facts.excerpt: Our guide Edso offers bio-tours of the park
